'''Mark Alun Lewis''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} (born 7 December 1962) is the Gilbert and Betty Kennedy Chair in [[Mathematical Biology]] at the [[University of Victoria]],  [[professor emeritus]] and former [[Canada Research Chair]] of [[mathematical biology]] in the Department of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences and Department of Biological Sciences at the [[University of Alberta]].<ref>[http://www.math.ualberta.ca/~mlewis/ University of Alberta Home Page]</ref>  Among other topics, he has written extensively on the [[Allee effect]], [[invasive species]], [[parasitism]], and biological dispersal.<ref>[https://scholar.google.ca/citations?user=l_jCNmMAAAAJ Google Scholar Profile]</ref>

Mark Lewis completed a B.Sc. with a double major in biology and a combined major in mathematics and computer science at the [[University of Victoria]] in 1987, where he worked with [[Pauline van den Driessche]]. He earned his Ph.D. in mathematical biology from [[Oxford University]] in 1990. After obtaining his Ph.D., he spent a year at the [[University of Washington]] as an NSERC postdoctoral research associate, and then became an assistant professor at the [[University of Utah]] in 1992.

In 2015, he was elected as a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]].<ref>[https://uofa.ualberta.ca/news-and-events/newsarticles/2015/september/two-professors-earn-royal-society-honours University of Alberta Press Release]</ref>
He was elected as a fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] in 2017, "for contributions to mathematical biology and the study of spatial dynamics processes".<ref>[http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2017 SIAM Fellows: Class of 2017], retrieved 2017-04-25.</ref>
In 2018 the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] listed him in their inaugural class of fellows.<ref>{{citation|url=https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2018/Fellows|title=Canadian Mathematical Society Inaugural Class of Fellows|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society|date=December 7, 2018|access-date=January 7, 2020|archive-date=January 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122125232/https://www2.cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2018/Fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2025/05/new-fellows/ |access-date=2025-05-22 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>
